ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of every partner, beneficial owner, authorized representative, signatory, and material counterparty against: (i) the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List; (ii) the UN Security Council Consolidated List; (iii) the Hong Kong financial sanctions lists administered by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority and the Commerce and Economic Development Bureau; (iv) the People's Bank of China and Ministry of Foreign Affairs restrictive measures; and (v) domestic and foreign politically exposed persons registries. Enhanced due diligence is required for any PEP, immediate family member, or close associate, including source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence for the dried goji berry and herbal botanical wholesale trade. Screening must be repeated at formation, before any ownership change, on each SWIFT TT or wire transfer, and quarterly thereafter; automated alerts must be reviewed by the compliance officer before any irreversible transaction is executed.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Hong Kong Companies Registry e-Registry and ICRIS (Integrated Companies and Limited Partnerships Information System) name search portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under Hong Kong law, the entity may adopt an English name, a Chinese name, or both. English names must use Roman characters; Chinese names must use Traditional Chinese characters. Foreign-sourced names require phonetic transliteration or an approved romanized version for cross-border consistency with the PRC parent entity. For the PRC foreign-invested partnership parent, the four-tier naming convention applies: administrative division plus distinctive mark plus industry description plus organization form. For the Hong Kong vehicle, an English company name must end with Limited and a Chinese company name must end with the two-character corporate suffix equivalent; a limited partnership must include Limited Partnership or L.P. and must not be identical or confusingly similar to a name already registered on the Companies Registry index.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Companies Registry rejects a proposed name, the applicant receives a written refusal identifying the conflicting or prohibited statutory ground. Within 21 days of the refusal date, the applicant may file a written appeal with the Companies Registry, attaching the original name reservation application, the registry refusal notice, a sworn statutory declaration of prior use or authorization, and evidence of any ministerial or regulatory consent obtained for sensitive tokens. The Registrar must reconsider the matter on the papers. If the internal reconsideration is unsuccessful, the applicant may seek judicial review in the Court of First Instance within 42 days of the reconsideration decision. A reserve alternative name may be submitted simultaneously without waiving the appeal rights.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Hong Kong law does not absolutely prohibit a virtual office for registration purposes, but the Inland Revenue Department and Hong Kong banks will reject a pure commercial mailbox for an entity engaged in international bulk export of dried goji berries and herbal botanicals. A registered office may be a licensed corporate service provider address if the provider offers a physical serviced suite, on-site reception, meeting rooms, a dedicated Hong Kong contact, and evidence of authority to accept legal process. However, for this industry, banks require demonstrable commercial substance, including place of effective management, independent decision-making, personnel presence, and supporting trade documents; a bare virtual address will fail bank account opening and may trigger IRD economic substance scrutiny.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist for unannounced inspection: (1) nameplate displayed at the physical registered office; (2) Business Registration Certificate and partnership or company registration certificate available; (3) statutory records, accounting books, purchase invoices, and shipping documents for dried goji berries preserved at the registered office or a notified alternative location; (4) an authorized partner, director, or employee present during business hours; (5) mail handling capability; (6) all licences and health-related permits for herbal botanical wholesale displayed or available for production. Quantified risk: below 5% for a conventional compliant office; approximately 20% for a professional serviced office with dedicated staff and meeting rooms; above 60% for a virtual-only mailbox with no personnel or records on site.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Partnership Ordinance (Cap 38) ss. 4-12; Limited Partnerships Ordinance (Cap 37) ss. 4-10; Business Registration Ordinance (Cap 310) ss. 5-7; Import and Export Ordinance (Cap 60) ss. 3-6; Food Safety Ordinance (Cap 612) ss. 5-10; Chinese Medicine Ordinance (Cap 549) ss. 114-120
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Business Registration Office, Inland Revenue Department, HKSAR; for limited liability tier, Companies Registry (Registry of Limited Partnerships)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Business Registration Application (Form IRC 1) and, if elected, Form LP-1 (Application for Registration of a Limited Partnership)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. Under Hong Kong Partnership Ordinance, there is no minimum paid-up capital and no blocked escrow account requirement for a Foreign-Invested Partnership. Initial capital is determined in the partnership agreement, must be deposited into the partnership bank account as evidenced by a capital schedule, and non-resident partners may own 100% without foreign equity cap.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, at the first meeting of the General Partner and Management Committee of the Foreign-Invested Partnership (FIP), duly convened on [date] at the registered office, that: 1. The Foreign-Invested Partnership Agreement dated [date], together with its Schedules, is hereby approved, adopted, and ratified, and each partner is directed to make the capital contribution set opposite his or her name in the capital contribution schedule attached as Schedule A; such contributions constitute the initial subscribed capital of the FIP and shall be held for the partnership business only. 2. The registered office of the FIP shall be at [address], Hong Kong SAR, until lawfully changed, and such address shall be the official place for service of legal process, correspondence, and statutory filings. 3. The banking mandate of the FIP is hereby established with [bank name], and [Name], [Name], and [Name] are appointed as authorized signatories, with any two to act together, to open, operate, and maintain current, foreign currency, and SWIFT-enabled accounts, to execute banking contracts, and to approve all telegraphic transfers, wire transfers, trade payments, and receipts relating to the international, wholesale and bulk export of dried goji berries and herbal botanicals. 4. [Name] is appointed as the Principal Statutory Officer, [Name] is appointed as the AML and Compliance Officer, and [Name] is appointed as the Partnership Secretary for the purposes of the Partnership Ordinance, the Business Registration Ordinance, and all applicable licensing statutes. 5. The appointed officers are jointly and severally authorized to prepare, execute, and file all documents, returns, declarations, and applications with the Companies Registry, Inland Revenue Department, Customs and Excise Department, Food and Environmental Hygiene Department, Department of Health Chinese Medicine Regulatory Office, Environmental Protection Department, and Fire Services Department, including but not limited to business registration, food trader registration, Chinese herbal medicines trader licence, export licences, warehouse fire safety certificates, and environmental clearances. 6. The officers may engage external solicitors, accountants, notaries, customs brokers, and banks as necessary; the financial year shall end on [date]; and this resolution shall remain in full force and effect until revoked by a written resolution of the partners.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-formation Name Clearance and Trade Name Availability Check
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry (Name Search Section) and Business Registration Office, Inland Revenue Department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name clearance at the relevant Hong Kong registries before filing any formation instrument. The proposed English name and, if desired, Chinese trade name of the Foreign-Invested Partnership must be submitted through the Companies Registry name search function and screened against the Business Registration Office trade-name database. If the name is identical to or confusingly similar to an existing registered entity, choose an alternative name or obtain a written consent letter from the prior owner. Prepare a name-clearance memorandum recording the search date, database used, search result, and final name selected. This memorandum will also support the availability declaration made in the Form IRC 1 business registration application.
required_dossiers: Brief scope of business in English
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected due to similarity, immediately submit an alternative name or file the consent letter of the existing entity; if the registry raises a formal query, respond with a written explanation within seven business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Foreign-Invested Partnership Agreement and Governance Instruments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Hong Kong solicitor and notary public; partner-side counsel for foreign investors
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a Hong Kong solicitor to draft the Foreign-Invested Partnership Agreement in accordance with the Partnership Ordinance (Cap 38). The agreement must fix the capital contributions, profit-sharing ratio, management authority, registered office address, banking mandate, statutory officer appointments, dispute resolution mechanism, and admission or withdrawal of partners. Circulate the draft for negotiation and execute the final deed before a witness. For non-resident partners, evidence of legal existence, including certificate of incorporation, certificate of incumbency, passport copies, and board resolution authorizing the partnership investment, must be notarized and apostilled as required. The executed agreement and all supporting constitutional documents must be retained in the statutory records.
required_dossiers: Passport copies or good standing certificates of all partners
Notarized and apostilled partner authorization documents
Consent letter for registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the agreement is rejected by a bank or registry due to defective provisions, execute an amendment deed and re-notarize; if a foreign partner's documentation lacks necessary legalization, arrange for apostille and consular certification before re-filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration with the Inland Revenue Department
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Business Registration Office, Inland Revenue Department, HKSAR Government
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and file Form IRC 1 with the Business Registration Office within one month after the partnership commences business. The form must set out the registered business name, address of principal place of business, nature of business (ISIC 4631 wholesale of food and botanical products), date of commencement, and particulars of each partner. Attach the executed partnership agreement and certified identity documents. Pay the prescribed business registration fee plus levy. Upon approval, the Business Registration Officer issues the Business Registration Certificate, which must be displayed at all business premises. Renew the certificate periodically and file any change of partnership particulars with the office within one month of such change.
required_dossiers: Business registration fee and levy payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried or suspended, furnish a corrected Form IRC 1 within 14 days; if late filing penalties are imposed, request mitigation by writing to the Business Registration Office with a full explanation and verified date of commencement.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Optional Registration as Limited Partnership for Liability Shield
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry, Registry of Limited Partnerships
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If the partners require a protective limitation of liability for non-managing investors, file Form LP-1 with the Companies Registry for registration as a limited partnership under the Limited Partnerships Ordinance (Cap 37). The filing must include an executed limited partnership deed listing the general partner and all limited partners, a statement of particulars, and a statutory declaration by the general partner confirming compliance with the ordinance. The general partner must be personally liable for partnership obligations, while limited partners may not participate in management without losing limited liability. If all requirements are met, the Registrar issues the Limited Partnership Registration Certificate; update the registered particulars whenever the identity, address, capital contribution, or share of any partner changes.
required_dossiers: Statement of particulars of general and limited partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Registry queries the deed or declaration, amend the document with solicitor's advice and re-file; if the name conflicts, change the partnership name first; if the declaration is incomplete, supply a further statutory declaration and pay any correction fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Activation and Statutory Officer Record Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed bank in Hong Kong; Companies Registry and Financial Services and Treasury Bureau for AML registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a multi-currency business bank account in the exact legal name of the Foreign-Invested Partnership. The bank requires the Business Registration Certificate, the Limited Partnership Registration Certificate (if any), the executed partnership agreement, the first board/governing resolution approving the banking mandate, identification, address proof and source of wealth for all partners and ultimate beneficial owners, and a projected trade projection for the dried goji berry and herbal botanical business. The bank will conduct AML/CTF due diligence, sanction screening, and credit checks. Once the account is opened, record the SWIFT/BIC, account numbers, and signatory cards in the statutory register. Submit any necessary beneficial ownership and business activity notifications to the Business Registration Office and complete the statutory officer records.
required_dossiers: Beneficial ownership and source of wealth declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank issues an AML/KYC query, provide supplemental bank statements, tax returns, or third-party documentation proving the legitimacy of capital; if the application is declined, appeal to the bank AML compliance committee or submit a revised application to another licensed bank.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Food and Environmental Hygiene Department (FEHD); Department of Health Chinese Medicine Regulatory Office / Chinese Medicines Board; Environmental Protection Department (EPD); Fire Services Department (FSD)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Food Importer and Distributor Registration under Food Safety Ordinance (Cap 612); Wholesale Food Business Registration under Food Business Regulation (Cap 132X); Chinese Herbal Medicines Trader Licence under Chinese Medicine Ordinance (Cap 549) for herbal botanicals; Export Licence under Import and Export Ordinance (Cap 60) for international bulk export; Warehouse Fire Safety Certificate for storage premises

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Department (EPD), Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt. The proposed wholesale, warehousing, and international bulk export of dried goji berries and herbal botanicals does not constitute a designated project under Schedule 2 of the Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance (Cap 499) and therefore no EIA report or environmental permit is required. If the operator later adds chemical fumigation, cold storage using ammonia, or packaging/assembly processes with solvents, a fresh EIA screening and environmental licence under the Air Pollution Control Ordinance (Cap 311) or Water Pollution Control Ordinance (Cap 358) will be required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater will be generated; any stormwater or trade effluent discharged from the warehouse rainwater system must comply with the Water Pollution Control Ordinance limits, including pH 6-9, BOD5 not exceeding 30 mg/L, and suspended solids not exceeding 30 mg/L. No open burning of packaging waste is permitted; waste must be collected by licensed waste collectors. For dried goji berries and herbal botanicals, sulphur dioxide residue must not exceed 50 ppm; pesticide residues must comply with the Pesticide Residues in Food Regulation (Cap 132CM); and heavy metal limits for Chinese herbal medicines, where applicable, are mercury not exceeding 0.2 mg/kg, arsenic not exceeding 2.0 mg/kg, and cadmium not exceeding 1.0 mg/kg.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain a fire service installation certificate from the Fire Services Department before warehouse occupancy, together with a valid structural safety certificate for storage racking from a registered structural engineer. The premises must comply with the Fire Safety (Commercial Premises) Ordinance (Cap 502), including approved means of escape, emergency lighting, exit signs, fire detection and alarm systems, and fire-fighting equipment. If fumigants or flammable solvents are stored, a Dangerous Goods Licence must be issued by the Fire Services Department. Workplace safety clearance under the Occupational Safety and Health Regulation (Cap 509) is required, including first-aid kits, safety training, and employer's compensation insurance for all workers.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA) using the national electronic tax service platform (Electronic Tax Bureau / e-Tax portal); for the Hong Kong SAR segment, the Inland Revenue Department of Hong Kong SAR (IRD) using the eTAX electronic filing portal remains separately competent, but the mainland-registered Foreign-Invested Partnership files its primary registration with the STA.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Complete market-regulatory incorporation of the Foreign-Invested Partnership with the Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) and obtain the Unified Social Credit Code, which is the official national tax identification number (TIN) for the FIP. Step 2: File the initial tax registration through the STA Electronic Tax Bureau / e-Tax portal within 30 days of the business licence date, submitting the partnership agreement, foreign investor identity documents, registered address proof, and expected business scope. Step 3: Elect VAT taxpayer status in the e-Tax system; apply for general VAT-taxpayer status if required by scale or to support export zero-rating and input-VAT refunds. Step 4: If a foreign non-resident partner is not separately tax-registered in mainland China, obtain a non-resident counterparty registration / withholding reference number through the e-Tax platform for withholding income tax on China-source income; this is separate from the FIP TIN. Step 5: Register with China Customs through the Single Window and obtain the Customs-export registration reference; link the customs filing to the STA VAT registration for export declaration and VAT-rebate processing. Step 6: For the Hong Kong trading/hub leg, ensure the HK buyer or related HK entity holds a valid Hong Kong Business Registration Certificate with the IRD under the one-stop business registration system, as this supports the offshore sale chain and cross-border documentation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible; under PRC partnership tax rules, the FIP is transparent for Enterprise Income Tax and does not pay entity-level EIT; each corporate or individual partner is taxed on its distributive share, while VAT applies at the FIP level on taxable mainland supplies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None; PRC domestic law has no check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch elections for a Foreign-Invested Partnership; transparent classification is mandatory, and partners may separately claim foreign tax credits or Mainland-Hong Kong double taxation arrangement relief.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: People's Republic of China Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the PRC Value-Added Tax Law and implementing regulations; Hong Kong SAR has no separate VAT/GST/sales tax, and PRC VAT applies to the FIP's mainland supply and export-sale transactions based on goods shipped from mainland customs territory.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: RMB 5,000,000 (five million Chinese Yuan) of annual aggregate taxable sales is the mandatory turnover threshold for general VAT taxpayer registration; the FIP must still obtain its Unified Social Credit Code/TIN upon incorporation irrespective of turnover, and may apply to become a general VAT taxpayer voluntarily to support zero-rated export refunds.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: The FIP must issue all VAT invoices through the State Taxation Administration's fully digitalised electronic invoice service platform under Golden Tax Phase IV; invoice data, sales data, and VAT returns are transmitted to the tax authority in real time; every invoice is digitally stamped with a tax-control seal and anti-counterfeiting QR code before issue; high-volume exporters use mandatory system-to-system integration with the STA platform and China Customs Single Window to match export declarations, VAT invoices, and foreign-exchange receipts.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available where the FIP is a registered general VAT taxpayer and exports dried goji berries (Lycium) or herbal botanicals physically out of mainland China customs territory to an offshore buyer, including goods exported to Hong Kong SAR for re-export or onward international sale, and the export is evidenced by a Chinese Customs Export Declaration, commercial invoice, transport documentation, and foreign-currency payment receipt; the goods must leave mainland customs control and be sold in export trade; offshore services are not in this entity's scope.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Chinese Customs Export Declaration (customs clearance declaration for export goods)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical exit from mainland China customs territory
Export sales contract and commercial invoice
Bank-generated foreign exchange receipt / foreign exchange income declaration record evidencing repatriation and settlement of the export proceeds
VAT invoice for the export sale as issued through the fully digitalised e-invoice system
Export tax rebate/zero-rating application filed through the STA Electronic Tax Bureau / e-Tax portal and linked to the China Customs Single Window declaration
Certificate of Origin and phytosanitary/health certification for dried goji berries/herbal products where required by the importing jurisdiction
Hong Kong import/export documentation (such as Hong Kong Customs import/export declaration or movement permit) where the goods are transshipped through Hong Kong
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: China Customs and the STA jointly audit export zero-rating and refund claims by cross-matching customs declarations, e-invoices, VAT returns, and foreign-exchange receipts under Golden Tax Phase IV. If export zero-rating is obtained or claimed on the basis of false declarations, circular exports, fabricated transport documents, unverified payments, or failure to repatriate and settle export proceeds within the prescribed 180-day foreign-exchange collection period, the tax authority will disallow the claim, claw back the VAT exemption or refund, impose late-payment surcharges, and apply penalties under the Law on the Administration of Tax Collection and tax evasion rules ranging from 50 percent to 500 percent of the improper tax amount; fraudulent export-rebate conduct may also be prosecuted under the PRC Criminal Law as export tax rebate fraud, with loss of export-rebate status and potential custody/property penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) for the Hong Kong SAR treasury layer, together with the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) under the People's Bank of China for the mainland China Foreign-Invested Partnership (FIP) layer
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region operates a fully convertible HKD and imposes no distinction between current-account and capital-account convertibility for treasury transactions; all legitimate FX transactions may be executed at market-determined rates under the Linked Exchange Rate System. For the underlying PRC Foreign-Invested Partnership, current-account items such as cross-border trade payment and service fees are broadly convertible after bank verification, while capital-account inflows such as paid-in capital from the Hong Kong limited partner require Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) registration with SAFE and a designated capital account. Profit distribution and dividend/partnership-profit remittances from the PRC FIP to Hong Kong limited partners require a certified audit report, tax clearance certificate, and bank-level proof that the distributed profits were generated by the registered PRC business. Although the Hong Kong layer faces no surrender or repatriation restrictions, the onshore leg still faces practical hurdles because banks apply substance-over-form safeguards and simultaneous customs and tax matching for dried lycium/herbal wholesale exports. Overall, the route is workable, but the capital account approvals and FX purpose-code integrity must be independently documented to avoid anti-circumvention sanctions under SAFE Notice 2019-28.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the current SAFE foreign-exchange framework, there is no mandatory conversion ratio; the exporter may retain up to 100% of foreign currency receipts in a foreign-exchange settlement account or convert them into RMB at the prevailing market rate. Export proceeds from dried goji berries and herbal botanicals must be repatriated into China through the designated receiving bank and be included in the trade-monitoring system. The bank must complete verification within 90 days after the customs export declaration; if collection occurs more than 90 days after shipment, the exporter must provide a written delay explanation and supporting evidence such as transport documents, buyer payment undertaking, or bank reference. In the Hong Kong treasury layer, no statutory surrender requirement or conversion ratio applies.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: The Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corporation Limited (HSBC)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational Currency Account and Multi-Currency Treasury Account
Capital Escrow Account and Foreign Currency Settlement Account
Basic Operational Currency Account and Trade Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Fintech EMI cross-border viability is Low-to-Medium for the Hong Kong treasury layer and Low for the PRC FIP layer. HKMA-licensed virtual banks and stored value facilities are legally able to provide transaction accounts to Hong Kong-incorporated vehicles, but they generally cannot open a SAFE-registered capital account or render commercial documentary trade services for a mainland Foreign-Invested Partnership. Offshore EMIs such as Airwallex, Currencycloud, and Revolut Business are not licensed deposit-taking institutions in mainland China and are legally barred from acting as the primary treasury rail for the onshore FIP; they may only serve as ancillary collection dashboards for small remote receivables once the primary licensed bank spine is active. The prudent design is to keep all capital account, FX conversion, LC, and documentary collection activity inside Tier-1 licensed banks and use any HKMA-authorised EMI strictly as a downstream e-commerce collection overlay.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Statutory directors and general partners of the FIP must attend a physical in-branch interview at the relevant Tier-1 Bank. Remote consular proxy account opening is not generally accepted for a cross-border FIP with a China-Hong Kong dual layer because HKMA and SAFE-covered banks require biometric verification of the general partner and at least one authorised authorised signatory. For the Hong Kong-incorporated treasury partner, on-boarding typically permits the Hong Kong partner director and corporate secretary to attend in Hong Kong, while the mainland managing partner can attend at the bank's designated China desk or Hong Kong office if transportation and visa logistics are synchronised. The bank will request original passports, Hong Kong identity cards, mainland ID cards, partnership registration certificates, certificate of incorporation, business registration certificate, and original power-of-attorney forms before accepting any account mandate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque beneficial ownership structure caused by the combination of a Hong Kong offshore special-territory layer and a PRC Foreign-Invested Partnership with no minimum capital requirement.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the complete partnership register; signed partnership agreement; capital contribution schedule; passports and proof of residential address for every individual partner; certificate of incumbency from the Hong Kong registered agent; corporate registry search reports for all intervening HK companies; audited financial statements or certified net-worth statements; source-of-wealth letters and six-month bank statements evidencing fund accumulation; and a notarised declaration confirming no undisclosed nominee partners.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Commodity classification and sanctions screening ambiguity for dried lycium berries and herbal botanicals, as the term 'herbal' can trigger phytosanitary, narcotics-precursor, and dual-use agricultural review procedures.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver a product dossier with exact HS codes and international botanical nomenclature; supplier and offtake contracts; phytosanitary certificate; certificate of origin; independent laboratory composition and heavy-metal report; Chinese customs export declaration; packing list and bill of lading; cargo insurance policy; end-user certificate or buyer license where relevant; and SWIFT counterparty screening results showing no adverse OFAC, UN, EU, or HKMA sanctions matches.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade invoice and currency mismatch red flags in bulk herbal wholesale flow, especially when FIP invoices move from onshore supplier to Hong Kong treasury vehicle and then to overseas buyer, raising over/under-invoicing and transfer-pricing AML concern.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the full tiered transaction chain: onshore purchase contract, Hong Kong resale contract, commercial invoices with Incoterms, customs declarations and valuation reports, independent commodity price benchmark quotations, bank payment confirmations with SAFE transaction purpose codes, SWIFT MT103 payment trails, container and logistics waybills, warehouse delivery receipts, and annual transfer-pricing documentation prepared under arm's-length principles.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Pass-through partnership structure and zero minimum capital outlay create economic-substance and shell risk, potentially disqualifying the FIP from commercial banking facilities.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit a substance file comprising HK office lease with physical signage photos; payroll records for resident staff; partnership meeting minutes and resolutions; a detailed business plan with projected export volume; warehouse or logistics contracts in the relevant jurisdiction; customs bond and trade licenses; prior tax returns and employment returns; employer and director appointment records; and a treasury management policy explaining expected monthly volume and clearing activity in the Tier-1 account.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The inbound capital injection from the Hong Kong limited partner to the PRC FIP must be executed as a SWIFT MT103 wire into the FIP's designated SAFE-registered capital account at a licensed designated bank. The remittance instruction must state the exact corporate name of the FIP as beneficiary and include the FX transaction purpose code 622011 for paid-in capital of a foreign-invested enterprise. The Hong Kong remitting entity must ensure the SWIFT sender name matches the registered company certificate, and the FIP must complete Foreign Investment Information Reporting through the AMEIZ-style integrated investment management system before the wire arrives. After funds are credited, the receiving bank issues an inbound capital account confirmation and performs capital verification against the partnership's capital contribution schedule, the signed partnership agreement, and the notarised registration certificate. If the capital is retained as foreign currency, it may be deposited into a foreign currency capital account; if RMB is required for operating expenses, the bank will conduct a lawful capital settlement transaction and monitor the funds under SAFE anti-circumvention scrutiny.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements for the dried goji berries and herbal botanicals business should use a layered clearing approach. For direct sales to overseas buyers, SWIFT MT103 is the primary rail for settlement of export proceeds identified against a commercial invoice and customs declaration. For larger or formally financed orders, a confirmed irrevocable commercial letter of credit should be issued by the buyer's bank and advised through one of the Tier-1 HK relationship banks, with settlement made against compliant shipping documents and in line with UCP600. For smaller wholesale or repeat consignment transactions, documentary collections on a documents-against-payment or documents-against-acceptance basis are permissible, with the presenting bank handling the bills of lading, invoices, packing lists, phytosanitary certificates, and certificates of origin before releasing documents. Any bank-to-bank reimbursement between the collecting and remitting institutions should be processed by SWIFT MT202 cover instructions, and the treasury desk must maintain a matching file linking each outgoing disbursement to the related import or export trade file to support FATF, HKMA, and SAFE audit expectations.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards up to 12 months in USD/CNH and USD/HKD for hedging identifiable trade receivables and payables
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on USD/CNY/CNH limited to balance-sheet hedging of capital injection and profit remittance exposure, not for speculative positions
Cross-currency swaps (USD/HKD/CNH) collateralised under ISDA/CSA for matching the FIP's capital-account asset-liability mismatch
European-style vanilla FX options for hedging procurement cost volatility in herbal wholesale trades, with documented underlying trade exposure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Business Registration Office, Inland Revenue Department
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after the expiry of the current Business Registration Certificate, which is issued for a validity period of one year from commencement of business and renewed annually on the anniversary of the registration date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal incurs a penalty of HKD 300 (USD 38.46) if filed within one month after expiry, escalating to HKD 1,000 (USD 128.21) thereafter; continued default may lead to prosecution, removal from the Business Register, and the partnership being treated as unregistered, which renders its business operations unlawful

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after the anniversary of the registration of the limited partnership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file within the prescribed period incurs a default fine of HKD 105 per month of default, up to a maximum of HKD 5,000 (USD 641.03); in addition, the Registrar may strike the partnership off the register if the annual return remains outstanding for two consecutive years, leading to dissolution of the partnership

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month from the date of issue (typically issued on the first working day of April); extensions may be granted to 15 August or 15 November for financial years ending on 31 December depending on whether accounts are prepared by a tax representative
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties range from HKD 1,200 (USD 153.85) for an initial offence to HKD 10,000 (USD 1,282.05) and imprisonment of up to three months for persistent default; the IRD may also issue estimated assessments based on deemed profits without allowance for deductions, causing higher tax liability

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month from the date of issue, normally issued on the first working day of April; an employer with no employees must still complete and return the nil declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties of HKD 1,200 (USD 153.85) for the first offence, escalating to HKD 10,000 (USD 1,282.05) and imprisonment for up to three months; failure to file may also result in a penalty for undercharging of tax and adverse action in subsequent prosecution

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Hong Kong Limited Partnerships Ordinance and Business Registration Ordinance, no statutory audit is required for a limited partnership engaged in wholesale trading (ISIC 4631) purely on the basis of balance sheet, turnover, or headcount thresholds. For comparative context, if this entity were structured as a private company limited by shares, the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) would mandate an audit unless it qualifies as a small company (turnover not exceeding HKD 20 million, total assets not exceeding HKD 10 million, and employees not exceeding 50) and all members approve the exemption. Partnerships, however, are expressly outside this regime. A compulsory audit by a certified public accountant would only arise if the partnership holds a regulatory license under the Securities and Futures Ordinance (e.g., Type 1 or Type 2 regulated activities), the Banking Ordinance, the Insurance Ordinance, or the Money Service Operators Ordinance, where client asset thresholds, transaction volumes, and licensing conditions impose audit obligations. Otherwise, audits are triggered solely by private contractual arrangements such as bank financing, partnership agreements, or investor requirements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Hong Kong Financial Reporting Standards (HKFRS) issued by the Hong Kong Institute of Certified Public Accountants (HKICPA), or HKFRS for Private Entities (SME Framework) if the entity meets the eligibility criteria for small private entities. The Inland Revenue Department generally accepts accounts prepared in accordance with HKFRS or a reasonable and consistent accounting basis that reflects the true profits of the partnership for tax assessment purposes.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Hong Kong does not impose a separate statutory beneficial ownership register or annual UBO confirmation filing on limited partnerships. The annual confirmation mechanism is satisfied through the filing of Form LP1 with the Companies Registry within one month after each anniversary, which must set out the full list of limited and general partners, their capital contributions, and any changes. Any transfer, admission, or retirement of a partner triggering a change in partnership interest must be reported using Form LP2 within 15 days of the change. For anti-money laundering compliance, the partnership is required to maintain up-to-date beneficial ownership information internally and provide it to law enforcement or regulatory authorities on request; however, there is no public or annual UBO filing beyond the annual return.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Limited Partners (including capital contributions and profit-sharing ratios)
Register of Charges (if any liabilities secured by partnership assets)
Record of Form LP2 Change Notifications (chronological log of partner changes)
Copy of the Limited Partnership Agreement and Certificate of Registration

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 400 - 2,000 per year, depending on whether a virtual office, physical address, and corporate secretarial support are provided
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 0 (no statutory audit required); if voluntarily audited for bank financing or as mandated by the partnership agreement, a typical certified audit fee ranges from USD 2,000 to 6,000 per audit cycle

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard PRC Enterprise Income Tax under Article 4 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law; the Foreign-Invested Partnership itself is fiscally transparent and is not a CIT payer, so each partner is taxed on the allocated share.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory patent box exists in the PRC. Reduced rates: 15% for qualifying High and New Technology Enterprises; 15% for encouraged industries in the Western Development regions; effective 2.5% to 5% rates for Small and Low-Profit Enterprises; 100% super deduction for eligible R&D expenses. For an FIP, all incentives and deductions are claimed at the partner level, not the partnership level, because the partnership is a pass-through entity.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Primary form for the corporate partner claimant: PRC Annual Enterprise Income Tax Return for Corporate Partners (CIT Form A100000 series filed by each partner, not by the FIP); for the Foreign-Invested Partnership itself, the mandatory return is the Partnership Income Allocation Statement and Non-Resident Partner Schedule (filed through the State Taxation Administration electronic tax filing system 'e-Taxation'). For non-resident partners claiming Mainland-HK DTA relief, the non-resident return is also supported by the Non-Resident Enterprise Income Tax Withholding Return.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual settlement plus quarterly prepayment of CIT by each corporate partner; annual filing of the FIP Partnership Income Allocation Statement; withholding and DTA relief filings for non-resident partners on each repatriation event and monthly/quarterly withholding return.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: CIT annual return is due within 5 months after the fiscal year-end, i.e., by May 31 for a calendar-year taxpayer. Quarterly CIT prepayments are due within 15 days after each quarter-end. Partnership allocation schedules and non-resident withholding returns are due by the 15th day of the month following the month in which the allocation or repatriation occurs.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 - Taxpayer Identification and Resident Status
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, Chinese social credit code of the FIP, partner tax registration number, type of partner (resident corporate, non-resident corporate, individual), and country/jurisdiction of residence.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mark the box for non-resident corporate partner as Hong Kong SAR resident. The FIP is not a CIT payer; do not file an entity-level CIT return in the FIP name. Ensure that the HK partner has a valid Hong Kong Tax Residency Certificate for treaty relief.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 - Fiscal Year and Accounting Period
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calendar year or approved fiscal year of the FIP and of each corporate partner.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Align the non-resident partner's reporting period with the FIP's annual accounting period. A mismatch between the HK partner's year-end and the PRC FIP's year-end can create double inclusion or deferred allocation issues and must be resolved with a contemporaneous allocation schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross receipts from international bulk export of organic dried goji berries and herbal botanicals, including sales, export revenue, commissions, and ancillary logistics service fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident partners, only China-source income is allocable. Do not net intercompany purchase or management fees against revenue without documentary support. Revenue from e-commerce export must be supported by export declarations and inbound wire records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of goods sold, procurement, warehousing, packaging, freight, herb quality testing, insurance, depreciation, and deductible operating expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reject intra-group charges that lack economic substance. Management fees allocated by an HK parent to the PRC FIP must satisfy the arm's length standard. If the HK partner charges royalties for botanical processing technology, the royalty must be capitalized or expensed only if the intangible asset is legally owned and the charging structure is at arm's length.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 - Pass-Through Allocation of FIP Taxable Income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income of the FIP after applying the 'first divide and then tax' rule; allocation to each partner according to the partnership profit-sharing ratio.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the HK corporate partner's distributive share. Do not confuse cash distributions with taxable allocation: under PRC tax law, undistributed retained profits are still allocated and taxed to partners. For a non-resident partner, if the partnership operates through a permanent establishment in China, the allocated share is business profit attributable to the PE and taxable at 25% net basis under Article 7 of the Mainland-HK DTA. If no PE is established and the DTA applies, the China-source business profit may not be taxed in China; however, PRC anti-abuse rules will re-examine whether the HK partner in fact has substance and control.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Adjustments for tax-exempt government grants, qualified interest, penalties, and non-deductible expenditures, plus transfer pricing adjustments raised by the tax authority.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A HK partner cannot claim PRC income tax exemptions for partnership profits that have been allocated from a PRC FIP unless a specific treaty provision applies. If the tax authority makes a transfer pricing adjustment increasing FIP profits, the additional tax is allocated to the non-resident partner according to the same profit-sharing ratio.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 - Taxable Income and Tax Rate
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compute partner-level taxable income after loss carryforwards and incentives.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a resident corporate partner, apply the 25% rate or a preferential 15% rate if qualified. For a non-resident HK corporate partner with a PRC PE, apply the 25% rate on the net PE profit; do not apply the 10% gross-basis withholding rate to PE-attributable business profits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 - Withholding Tax on Non-Resident Partner
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: If the FIP distributes profits to the HK partner as China-source income not attributable to a PE, the FIP is the withholding agent and must withhold and report on a gross-basis.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Domestic withholding is 10% under Article 37 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law if the HK partner is treated as deriving China-source non-PE income. Mainland-HK DTA may override the domestic rate only after a proper DTA application. Partnership profit allocations are not automatically 'dividends' for DTA purposes; the proper treaty category is usually business profits (Article 7) if a PE exists. If the arrangement is characterized as a dividend-like distribution from an investment in the FIP, the 5% DTA dividend rate is not available merely because the partner is a HK company; direct shareholding of 25% is required only for shares in a PRC resident company, not for a partnership interest.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 9 - Foreign Tax Credits and Treaty Credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claims for foreign taxes paid in Hong Kong or other jurisdictions against PRC tax liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident HK partner generally has no PRC foreign tax credit entitlement except under the DTA and domestic unilateral credit rules. The HK partner must file the corresponding Hong Kong Profits Tax return and cannot use a unilateral PRC credit for taxes paid in HK unless the income is also sourced in PRC. Maintain source evidence to avoid double taxation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 10 - Tax Incentives, Loss Carryforward and Prior-Year Adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Loss carryforward deductions, R&D super deductions, preferential plant or equipment deductions, and credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The FIP itself is not an 'enterprise' for most CIT incentive regimes. Deductions are only claimable by the partner that bears the economic burden. A non-resident corporate partner without a PRC PE may not claim R&D super deductions or the small-and-low-profit rate. Loss carryforward for a non-resident partner is limited to PRC PE-attributable losses and cannot be used against non-PRC income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Annual related-party transaction disclosure forms (controlled transaction schedules) covering purchases of dried goji berries, intercompany loans, management fees, intangible royalties, and service contracts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The PRC tax authority requires mandatory contemporaneous documentation and annual related-party forms once statutory thresholds are exceeded. The HK parent and the PRC FIP are connected parties; all cross-border payments must be consistent with the arm's length principle. The FIP must complete the transfer pricing schedule even if no tax is due, and the HK partner must produce the HK group's contemporaneous documentation if the PRC competent authority requests it.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 12 - Declaration, Digital Signature, and Responsible Person Certification
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Signature by the FIP's managing partner or legal representative, the corporate partner's tax officer, and the non-resident partner's authorized representative.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The person signing the return attests to truthfulness under penalty of perjury. For a non-resident partner, the authorized HK director must confirm beneficial ownership, HK tax residence, and absence of treaty abuse. Falsifying a beneficial ownership or residence certificate exposes the director to personal criminal liability and travel restrictions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the annual CIT return or partnership allocation statement: administrative fine of RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000, up to RMB 20,000 where the violation is serious, plus a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05% of unpaid tax from the statutory due date. Failure to file transfer pricing documentation: tax authority may disregard the documentation and impose an adjustment to taxable income with a penalty of up to 300% of the underpaid tax and the 0.05% daily surcharge. Withholding failures: under Article 69 of the Tax Collection and Administration Law, the FIP as withholding agent is liable for the unpaid tax, daily surcharge, and a fine from 50% to 300% of the amount that should have been withheld. Criminal tax evasion under Article 201 of the Criminal Law triggers fines and imprisonment for the persons directly in charge and other directly liable persons, with a maximum sentence of seven years in aggravated evasion cases. A published 'serious tax violation case' on the SAT blacklist also triggers exit bans and bank-account freezing.
